This script defines the helper functions the analysis scripts share. Three of them do work that usRds does not yet do, and are labelled "usRds gap" in the code. The [coverage assessment](usrds-coverage.qmd) explains each gap.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/functions.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/R/setup.R)

The functions are tested on synthetic data in [`tests/test-functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Fiorica-cryptoccoccus-analysis/blob/main/tests/test-functions.R). The code sections below are imported directly from the script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/functions.R")
```

## Codes for a concept

`codes_for_concept()` picks one concept's codes out of the `code_lists` table, and can limit them to one code type: diagnosis, procedure or HCPCS. It stops with an error if the concept name is misspelled, rather than silently returning no codes.

```{r}
#| label: codes-for-concept
#| eval: false
```

## Matching codes

`code_matches()` compares a vector of recorded codes with a code list. It handles both exact codes and prefixes, so the diabetes categories match their subcodes. The usRds `get_*_ICD()` functions match exactly only, which is why this exists (coverage step 6).

```{r}
#| label: code-matches
#| eval: false
```

## Searching wide code columns

The USRDS hospitalization files record each stay's codes in separate columns:

- the principal diagnosis, `PRIMDIAG`;
- secondary diagnoses `HSDIAG1` onwards (10 columns before 2010, 26 from 2010);
- procedures `HSSURG1` onwards.

`flag_codes_wide()` flags each row where any of the named columns holds a listed code. It skips columns a file does not have, so the same call works on both files (coverage steps 4–6 and 9).

```{r}
#| label: flag-codes-wide
#| eval: false
```

## Combining records into stays

A single hospital stay can appear as several hospitalization records. `collapse_stays()` puts a person's records in date order. It starts a new stay only when a record's admission date falls after the latest discharge date seen so far, so the stays it builds never overlap. A record admitted on the day of the previous discharge joins the same stay. The optional `gap_days` argument also joins records that start within that many days of discharge.

The function adds a stay identifier and the stay's first and last dates. The plan treats overlapping or contiguous records as one stay (§5); usRds has no equivalent (coverage step 7).

```{r}
#| label: collapse-stays
#| eval: false
```
